run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 21, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Between roughly 13:44 and 13:49 UTC on 2026-11-21 and continuing until about 14:45 UTC, the payment-api application in namespace app-100a failed to obtain database connections. In the Loki stream labeled job=payment-api, service=payment-api, pod_name=payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-l9lm4, namespace=app-100a, a level-filtered query for 13:30:00–13:49:30Z returned exactly one ERROR row, at 13:49:24Z; the 5-minute per-level counts for the namespace show DEBUG/INFO present from 10:52:48Z but the ERROR series first appearing in the window ending 13:49:36Z. The logged signature is 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20 and active_connections 20 and 7–46 waiting requests, 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' (error_code DB_CONN_001, stack at PaymentService.processPayment()/DatabasePool.acquire()), and '/healthz' responses of status_code 503 'Health check failed - database unreachable' taking 5009–9684 ms. A DEBUG query-duration line rises from 15–88 ms (12:30:17–13:34:45Z) to 1252 ms at 13:50:55Z. The last ERROR observed is the /healthz 503 at 14:44:44Z, and the 15-minute ERROR counts stop after the window ending 14:59:10Z. Some payments still completed normally during the burst (389 ms at 14:07:40Z, 323 ms at 14:09:43Z), so this was degradation, not a total outage. The deepest cause could not be assigned to a single object: the database payment-api talks to is not a visible workload in this cluster (no database Deployment, StatefulSet, Service, Endpoint or Pod; namespace app-219, named only by one stale endpoint event, does not exist), the application script and its pool configuration come from Secret payment-api-100a-script, which cannot be read, and Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable on every call, so metrics and traces could not be checked. No Kubernetes events for 2026-11-21 were returned (the events API covered only 2026-11-22T10:07:47–10:46:10Z), and the only payment-api pod now present was created 2026-11-22T10:46:09Z with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance, so pod state cannot describe the incident.

claims.text: In the payment-api stream of namespace app-100a on 2026-11-21, the only ERROR row the 13:30:00–13:49:30Z query returned is at 13:49:24Z: 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 27, wait_time_ms 17653.

Loki 5-minute counts by level for {namespace="app-100a"} from 10:52:48Z to 14:14:24Z on 2026-11-21 show DEBUG and INFO series from the start of the range, while the ERROR series begins with the window ending 13:49:36Z.

Across 13:35:00–14:15:00Z the payment-api stream logged three repeated error forms: 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' (pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 7 to 36, wait_time_ms 5216 to 22244), 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' with error_code DB_CONN_001 and stack 'at PaymentService.processPayment() ... at DatabasePool.acquire()', and 'Health check failed - database unreachable' on endpoint /healthz with status_code 503 and response_time_ms 5009 and 9684.

Sampled DEBUG 'Database query executed' durations for the payment-api pod were 15, 18, 30, 61, 65 and 88 ms between 12:30:17Z and 13:34:45Z and then 1252 ms at 13:50:55Z, the same second as a connection-acquisition error.

The same error signatures continued through 14:30–15:30Z (for example 14:30:57Z waiting_requests 46 wait_time_ms 26398 and 14:43:57Z wait_time_ms 26789); the last ERROR row observed is 'Health check failed - database unreachable' on /healthz with status_code 503 at 2026-11-21T14:44:44Z.

15-minute ERROR counts for {namespace="app-100a"} between 14:15:26Z and 19:59:50Z hold values only in windows ending at or before 14:59:10Z (last value 1), and no ERROR series is present for later windows of that range while DEBUG and INFO series continue to the end.

Some payment work succeeded during the burst: 'Payment processed successfully' with processing_time_ms 389 at 14:07:40Z and 323 at 14:09:43Z, interleaved with pool-exhaustion errors in the same stream.

Deployment payment-api-100a in namespace app-100a is at annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1 with 1 replica ready and available, and its single ReplicaSet payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 was created 2026-11-22T10:46:09Z; the container runs command [python /app/app-direct-push.py] from image python:3.9-slim with /app mounted from Secret payment-api-100a-script and a livenessProbe httpGet /healthz port 8080, periodSeconds 10, timeoutSeconds 10, failureThreshold 3.

The only payment-api pod present is payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-l9lm4, created 2026-11-22T10:46:09Z, phase Running and Ready, container payment-api restartCount 0 with empty lastState and running since 2026-11-22T10:46:10Z; this is state after the incident window, not during it.

The Kubernetes events view returned 13 events, all timestamped 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z to 10:46:10Z: Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started plus ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate and Deployment ScalingReplicaSet for loki and payment-api-100a in app-100a, and one Warning 'Endpoints' FailedToCreateEndpoint for app-219/mariadb at 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z stating 'endpoints "mariadb" already exists'.

The cluster's Deployment list (26 items) contains no database workload, the namespace list contains 8 namespaces and not app-219, the only StatefulSet is otel-demo/alertmanager, and the Service and Endpoints lists contain loki, kubernetes, kube-dns, metrics-server and the otel-demo services but no mariadb or database entry.

The otel-demo pod list shows prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn, container nginx, with restartCount 6 and a last termination reason Error and exit code 1, and kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz with restartCount 4 and last termination reason Error and exit code 2; all pods in otel-demo are phase Running and ready.

The payment-api process ran out of database connections because its backing database became slow or partially unreachable around 13:44–13:49Z: acquisition waits reached 5–27 s, active_connections stayed pinned at pool_size 20 across samples, /healthz reported 'database unreachable' with 503, and one sampled query took 1252 ms against 15–88 ms earlier; the database's own identity and health are not in the evidence, so which side degraded first is unknown.

A demand increase against the fixed 20-connection pool is an alternative explanation: waiting_requests ranged 7–46 while active_connections stayed at 20 in every sampled error line; request-rate and load metrics that would confirm or refute a traffic surge were unavailable, so this candidate stays open.

Because the liveness probe requests /healthz with timeoutSeconds 10 and failureThreshold 3, the observed 5.0–9.7 s 503 health-check responses could have triggered kubelet liveness restarts during the burst; no kubelet event, restart count or last-termination record for 2026-11-21 exists in this Run to test that.

The burst was not a total outage: successful payment lines with normal processing times (389 ms at 14:07:40Z and 323 ms at 14:09:43Z) appear interleaved with pool-exhaustion errors, so only part of the payment-api request handling failed.

No restart, OOMKilled or Evicted signature is readable on the payment-api workload: the current pod shows restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, and the Deployment has never moved past revision 1 with one ReplicaSet; this describes only the state at 2026-11-22T10:46–10:50Z.

A payment-api crash or crash-loop as the origin of the errors was rejected: the errors are application-level database-acquisition failures logged by a live process that was emitting healthy 15–88 ms query diagnostics before 13:45Z, and the readable pod state shows restartCount 0 with no last-termination record and no OOMKilled, Evicted, BackOff or Unhealthy evidence for this workload.

Inspect the backing database server payment-api uses (its connection limit, connection handling, latency and availability) for 2026-11-21T13:40–15:00Z, and review the pool_size and acquisition timeout values held in Secret payment-api-100a-script, since a 20-connection pool with up to 46 waiters cannot absorb a downstream slowdown.

Repair the metrics and tracing read paths so that error rates, latency and restart data can size the incident and separate a downstream database slowdown from a traffic surge; the nginx container of prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn shows restartCount 6 with last termination reason Error and exit code 1.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable on every call in this Run (execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, list_prometheus_rules and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error rates, latency histograms, app_payment_transactions_total, kube-state-metrics restart/replica series and any request-rate series could not be read for 2026-11-21; their values are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable on every call (traces_search and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so there is no span-level evidence of failed payment operations or of the downstream database calls they made.

Kubernetes events returned by the API covered only 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z to 10:46:10Z; no event for 2026-11-21 was delivered, so any kubelet liveness-probe failure, OOMKilled, Evicted or restart of the payment-api pod during the incident is unknown.

The payment-api application code and its connection-pool settings are mounted from Secret payment-api-100a-script, which cannot be read; the configured pool_size and acquisition timeout are unverified beyond the pool_size 20 printed in log lines.

The identity, host and health of the database payment-api connects to are unknown: no database Deployment, StatefulSet, Service, Endpoint or Pod exists in the cluster now, and namespace app-219 named in a 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z endpoint event does not exist; that event lies outside the incident window and was not tied to this cause.

No 2026-11-21 container logs are retained from the pod itself: the only pod, payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-l9lm4, was created 2026-11-22T10:46:09Z and the log read reported no previous container instance; incident logs exist only in the Loki stream labeled pod_name=payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-l9lm4.
The authorized window begins 2026-11-21T10:47:14Z, so earlier hours of 2026-11-21 were not queryable and the pre-incident baseline rests on 10:47–13:49Z only.

Views that returned no data state limits of this Run rather than health: f5f4aa4a-a2dc-41c8-9b3b-0f6e20efc323-t1:d89138ee-cfe1-4d2b-9cba-76b6d163ffd1 (payment-api pod logs, no previous container instance), 41fb4432-0f41-419f-a155-0abfdd79e516-t0:1adb660e-cafa-425c-8a8c-cd051aaca9ed (pods in namespace app-219, none returned), cd3abd36-0c41-4a17-abe6-147ab787d5b0-t1:168c1bde-7b22-4f55-87fd-6db5e0699390 (nginx logs of prometheus-readonly-proxy, none returned), 425335b5-ee5d-4642-8dee-1445f499adeb-t0:237c43c9-6927-40d7-8141-a0e9f84f9219 (NetworkPolicy query returned nothing), 425335b5-ee5d-4642-8dee-1445f499adeb-t1:dafa563e-0f0d-4f7b-9052-860e71aff76e (ResourceQuota query returned nothing) and 1cbb1f1e-4b4b-4c29-98d2-e4c49cd748b8-t0:209562b9-aefe-457c-82fa-ae954d185281 (ERROR log query for 20:00Z–10:47Z returned no lines); the state of NetworkPolicy, ResourceQuota and post-20:00Z logs in that timeframe is therefore unknown, not confirmed absent.
The change-history integration is not available in this Run, so whether any change touched the payment-api workload or its database around 13:45Z could not be checked.
next_steps: Identify and instrument the database that payment-api depends on (it is not a visible workload in this cluster) and inspect its server-side connection limit, errors and latency for 2026-11-21T13:40–15:00Z.
Read Secret payment-api-100a-script through an authorized channel to confirm the configured pool_size and acquisition timeout.

Restore or restart the metrics and tracing read paths, including the nginx container of prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn, so the log-only finding can be corroborated with error-rate and latency data.
If the degradation recurs, correlate it with incoming request volume to decide between a traffic surge and a downstream database slowdown before changing pool sizing.
